The Manager's Guide to EnPlace Pro

What you can see, what you can change, and where the read-only line is drawn — with every screen your account actually reaches.

01

What a Manager account can and can't do

Read-only on ordering. Surprisingly powerful on people.

The Manager role in EnPlace Pro is an oversight role. You see what's being spent and saved, and who ordered what — but you don't build orders and you don't hold supplier logins. What catches most people out is how much you can do: your team, and the product matching at your own restaurant.

You can see
Reports across every restaurant you're assigned to, full order history, order lists, supplier connection status, and the matched product lists.
You can change
Your team — invite people, change roles between Chef and Manager, reassign restaurants, remove members. Product matching at your own restaurant. And you can submit an order batch a chef already built.
You can't do
Create or edit an order, add or edit supplier logins, create order lists, change organization settings, or touch billing.
Why it works this way

Internally the app splits roles into operators (owner and chef — the people who create and change operational data) and everyone else. Managers sit deliberately outside that group. It means an order can never be placed by someone who isn't accountable for the kitchen it's going to, while you keep complete visibility over what was placed and what it cost.

What that looks like in the interface

WhereWhat's different for you
Top navigationNo + NEW ORDER button and no magnifying glass (Price Check)
Avatar menuNo Supplier Credentials, no Product Matching, no Billing, no Restaurants — but you do have Team
Restaurant selectorYour assigned restaurants only. There's no All Locations option
Order ListsYou can open and read them; the create and edit controls don't work for you
Order HistoryFull list, but no delete, no Receive, no Return to Checkout
ReportsEverything, unrestricted — but for one restaurant at a time
Watch out

A few buttons render for you and then silently redirect you back to the dashboard when clicked — New Order List is the usual one. That's the app's guard firing, not a broken page. Nothing you did caused it and nothing was saved.

02

Getting in

Accepting your invitation and signing in

Your owner invites you by email. The link in that email is one-time and creates your account.

  1. Click the link in the invitation email — they expire, so ask for a new one if it complains.
  2. Set your name and a password — eight characters minimum.
  3. Press Join Rossi Restaurant Group — the button shows your actual restaurant group name.
  4. You land on your dashboard with a short guided tour running.
Tip

If you were already invited as a chef and are now being made a manager, you don't get a new invitation — your existing account's role is simply changed, and the interface changes the next time you load a page.

03

Your guided tour

Five steps, and it's the only onboarding you get

The manager flow is short by design: a welcome, then Order History, Reports and Order Lists, then you're done. There's no setup phase and no supplier or ordering steps, because none of those are yours.

  • ← Back steps backwards; the × dismisses it.
  • Your avatar→Restart Tour runs it again any time.
  • It's desktop only — the tour doesn't appear on a phone.
04

Your dashboard

The financial picture across your restaurants
PanelWhat it's telling you
Hero tileSavings this month and the change against last month
Spend / Savings / Orders / Avg Order ValueThis month, with month-over-month movement
Spending TrendEight weeks of spend; toggle to Monthly for six months
Spending by RestaurantClick through to that restaurant's full report
Spending by SupplierClick through to that supplier's full report
Recent OrdersSupplier, restaurant, who ordered, amount, status — every row opens the order
Why it works this way

The dollar figures and the order table use deliberately different rules. Money only counts orders that actually went out; the Recent Orders table shows everything, including Price Changed orders still waiting on a decision. So an order can appear in the table and add nothing to Spend This Month. That's the app flagging unfinished business, not a miscalculation.

Switching restaurants

The dropdown at the top right holds the restaurants you've been assigned. Use it to move between them — every figure on the page follows.

Watch out

You are always looking at exactly one restaurant. Managers don't get the owner's All Locations option, and there's no combined view hiding anywhere: if no restaurant is explicitly selected the app quietly picks your first one. So if you oversee two sites, the dashboard total is one site's total, and the Spending by Restaurant panel will show the other one at $0.00 — that zero means “not the restaurant you're currently viewing”, not “no spending”. To compare the two, switch the dropdown and read them one at a time.

Two alerts can appear at the top of your dashboard. The first is a red banner — “Action required: N supplier connections need attention” — which means a supplier login has stopped working and nobody at that restaurant can order from it (see Checking supplier connections below). The second is aimed squarely at you:

Tip

Chefs never see this alert; owners and managers do. You can open each item and see what needs matching, but only an owner or a chef can actually create the match. Treat it as a list to hand over — or to raise at your next check-in with the owner.

05

Reports

The part of the app built for your job

Filtering

  • Date Range presets: Last 30/60/90 Days, plus This/Last Month, Quarter and Year. Choosing one applies immediately.
  • From and To for anything custom.
  • Restaurant narrows to one site — it only lists restaurants you're assigned to.
  • Every filter carries through when you click into a detail report.
Watch out

The default range is the last 30 days, not month-to-date. That's why these totals don't match the “this month” figures on your dashboard. Pick the This Month preset when you want them to line up — this trips up almost everyone the first time they reconcile the two.

Why it works this way

Only completed orders count in reports. Drafts, failed orders and unresolved price-changed orders are invisible here on purpose — reports are about money that actually moved.

The two savings views

Tip

Product Savings is the number that justifies the software. Missed Savings is the number that generates work — every row is either a matching gap or a habit worth changing. Bring the second one to your owner; fixing it needs their access.

If you get stuck

If Missed Savings shows Price comparison not available, no matched product lists exist yet for the restaurant you're viewing. The Go to Product Matching button does work for you — see the note below — but building a matched list from nothing is a big job, so this is usually one to hand to your owner.

Tip

You have more access to Product Matching than the menus suggest. There's no link to it in your avatar menu, but the pages aren't locked: reached by URL, or via that Go to Product Matching button, you can open a matched list at your own restaurant and fix matches — reassign a supplier's product, rename an item, remove a bad line. Only promoting or demoting an org-wide list is owner-only, and a list that's already promoted is read-only for everyone including your owner.

06

Drilling into a restaurant, supplier or person

Same three reports, three different lenses

Every row in the Reports tables is clickable, and each opens a full report of its own with your current filters preserved.

Use it to answerReport
Which site is spending more, and where the money goesRestaurant
Are we leaning too hard on one supplier, and how often do we orderSupplier
Who's ordering, how much, and are they taking the best pricesTeam member
Tip

The member report is the most useful one for coaching. Its Savings Left on the Table section is specific and actionable — it names the products where a cheaper supplier was sitting right there.

Watch out

Recent Orders inside a member report only shows completed orders inside the date range. If someone's list looks short, widen the range before assuming they haven't been ordering.

07

Order history

Everything placed across your restaurants
StatusMeaning
DraftBuilt but never submitted; expires 14 days after it was last opened
Price ChangedA supplier's price moved after the cart was built; waiting on a decision
Waiting to Submit / ProcessingQueued, or being placed with the supplier now
Completed / ConfirmedPlaced successfully
ReceivedSomeone marked it as physically delivered
FailedPlacement failed — the row explains why

You can filter by search text, supplier, status and date range, and open any order to see its line items, validation results and delivery date. Mark as Received doesn't render for you, and the delete cross appears but always fails.

Watch out

One exception is worth knowing, because it's easy to trigger by accident. A draft batch shows a Return to Checkout button, and that button works for you — it opens the review screen, where the batch submit button will actually place the orders. You can't build an order, but you can send one a chef left sitting in drafts. Check with them before you press it.

Watch out

Three quirks worth knowing before you reconcile anything:

1. The three KPI cards always mean “completed orders in the date range” and ignore the status filter. Filtering to Drafts leaves them unchanged.

2. Open work — drafts, failures, price changes — is always shown regardless of the date range, so a three-week-old draft appears in a seven-day window.

3. Cancelled orders are hidden unless you explicitly filter for them.

Tip

A Failed order shows no date, because it never got a submission timestamp. If a supplier swears they never received an order, filter to Failed first.

08

Order lists, read-only

Useful to look at, even though you can't edit them

Order lists are the reusable templates your chefs build orders from — Weekly Produce, Proteins, Dry Goods & Paper. They're shared per restaurant, so what you see is what the whole kitchen sees.

It's worth reviewing them occasionally. A list that's drifted out of date is one of the quieter causes of off-list ordering: if the products people actually need aren't on the list, they grab them mid-shift instead, and those grabs bypass price comparison.

Watch out

The star, the delete cross and the Edit buttons simply don't render for you. The one control that does appear and then fails is New Order List — clicking it returns you to the dashboard with no message. That's the app's guard firing, not a broken page.

09

The Team screen

The one place you have real write access

This surprises most managers: you have essentially the same powers as the owner here. You can invite, promote, demote, reassign and remove. Only Edit Organization is hidden from you.

Who can do this

Your avatar→Team — visible to owners and managers only.

Inviting someone

  1. Use the Invite Team Member panel on the right.
  2. Enter their email and pick Chef or Manager.
  3. Assign restaurants — a chef gets exactly one; a manager can have several.
  4. Press Send Invitation.
Tip

If the email doesn't arrive, the accept link is printed in grey under each pending invitation. Copy and send it directly.

Changing an existing member

  • Make Manager / Make Chef changes their role immediately.
  • Assign Restaurants → tick the boxes → Save Assignments.
  • Remove deactivates them and frees their seat.
  • There's no menu on the owner's row, or on your own.
Watch out

Seats are billed, and pending invitations count. The header shows something like 4/5 seats included; beyond the included five, each seat is an extra monthly charge on the owner's subscription. Cancel stale invitations rather than leaving them to occupy a paid seat.

Supplier requirements

Further down the same page is the Supplier Requirements grid — order minimums and case minimums per supplier, either as a single default or per restaurant. These are the rules that block an order from being submitted when it's too small. The grid saves the moment you type; there's no save button.

Watch out

Setting a Default value locks the per-restaurant cells in that row and discards any overrides already there. Check with your owner before changing these — they change what your chefs can submit.

10

Checking supplier connections

You can look, and you can usually re-validate

You can't add or edit supplier logins, but you can see their health — and a broken connection is one of the few things that will quietly stop your kitchens from ordering.

Who can do this

There's no link to this screen in your desktop menus. Two ways in: tap Suppliers on your phone dashboard, or bookmark /supplier_credentials on desktop. The page itself loads fine for you — it's just undiscoverable.

What you seeWhat it means
Active + ConnectedHealthy
Active + DisconnectedNormal for 2FA suppliers — the login is fine, the session lapsed
Failed / InvalidThe login stopped working. Prices are stale and nobody can order from this supplier
Awaiting CodeA verification code was sent and hasn't been entered yet
PendingJust added, still validating
If you get stuck

When a credential breaks, the effect downstream is subtle: an entire supplier's price column disappears from the order builder, and chefs report that a product “isn't available any more”. If several people report missing products at once, check this screen first.

Tip

Validate and Import work for you, on desktop and on your phone — re-validating a connection isn't operator-gated. That makes you the fastest fix for a lapsed session: press Validate, and if it's a 2FA supplier, ask whoever owns that login for the code. You still can't add or edit the credential itself.

11

EnPlace Pro on your phone

A smaller, sharper version of your dashboard

On a phone there's no top navigation at all. You get a three-tab bar at the bottom — Home, Order, Cart — and everything else is reached from your dashboard.

Getting around

ControlWhere it goes
View ReportsYour full reports
SuppliersSupplier connection health
Order HistoryEvery order across your restaurants
See allOrder history, from the Recent Orders card
Watch out

Three things to know about the phone experience as a manager:

1. The KPI strip scrolls sideways. There's a fourth figure — Avg Order — hidden off the right edge. Swipe it.

2. The Search quick link doesn't work for you. It points at Price Check, which is operator-only, so it bounces you back to the dashboard with no message.

3. There's no restaurant selector anywhere on mobile for managers. Your phone shows whichever restaurant the app picked, with no way to change it — so if you oversee two sites, use desktop whenever the answer depends on which one you're looking at.

12

When you need something you can't do

Who to ask, and exactly what to ask for

Most of the time you're blocked, it's by design rather than by error. This table turns the block into a specific request.

You need to…AskFor
Place or fix an orderA chef at that restaurant, or the ownerThey're the only ones who can create or edit orders
Add or repair a supplier loginThe owner, or the chef whose login it isCredentials belong to a person; only that person or an owner can change them
Fix a wrong price comparisonNobody — you can do thisProduct Matching has no menu link for you, but you can edit matches at your own restaurant
Add or rename a restaurantThe ownerRestaurant settings are owner-only
Change the plan, seats or paymentThe ownerBilling is owner-only
Create or edit an order listA chef at that restaurant, or the ownerLists are operator-only, though shared per restaurant

Reporting a problem well

Whatever the issue, four details make it solvable in one message instead of five:

  • The restaurant — almost everything in this app is scoped per site.
  • The supplier — most failures are one supplier's connection, not the whole app.
  • The order number if there is one, straight from Order History.
  • The exact message on screen, word for word.
Watch out

Changing anything here — even fixing a typo in your own name — requires your current password. It's the most common failed save on this screen. Nothing organizational lives here: not your role, not your restaurants, not supplier logins.

Click anywhere or press Esc to close
